title: In medina: numbers, prices and foreign words

blocks.text: Second week in Fès. Karīm Take Luca to the medina: the market, the shops, the taxi. Here the darija shows two characteristics that surprise those who come from Egyptian or Levantine: numbers (žuž for ...two, and the prices in ryal, not in dirham) and the many French and Spanish words, sometimes even Berber (amazigh), entered into the everyday language. In this unit you learn to understand numbers, prices and quantities, expressions of bargaining, the vocabulary of city and transport, and to recognize loans. As in MAG-01, the aim is to understand: production is limited to courtesy formulas and some essential demand (šḥal? () how much? Seven weeks, in parallel with B2-20, B2-21 and the beginning of B2-22.

rows: 9–10 hours · seven weeks (weeks 234–240), about 1,5 hours per week in two blocks

blocks.text: Materials This unit, a Moroccan speaker for scripts, authentic videos of markets and trips to Morocco chosen by the tutor
Targets. At the end of the unit you know:
1. understand Moroccan numbers from 1 a 1000, with the special features of         • two • and the tens;
2. understand the prices said in ryal and convert them to dirham;
3. follow negotiation and understand quantities and measures;
4. understanding the lexicon of medina and transport;
5. recognise loans from French, Spanish and amazigh.
Seven-week plan (two blocks from 40–45 minutes per week).

Two. In darija žuž , a word that does not exist in fuṣḥā nor in Egyptian: žuž d-l-ḫubzat "Two loaves', žuž Two boys are gonna die. The dual (ktabayn) exists only in a few words of time and measure: yumayn ʿamayn 2 years. The composite numbers are expressed by u . ḫəmsa u ʿəšrin "Twenty-five', "mya u' ḫəmsin "Centro 50a" Hours are often counted with the name of the number and article: f-t-təsʿud 9:00 a.m. f-l-woḥda 1-to-1 (MAG-01).

The official currency is the dirham (dərhəm, plural drahəm). But in the market, taxis and daily conversations many prices are said in ryal, a traditional unit of account: 1 dirham = 20 ryal, i.e. 1 ryal = 5 cents (santim). To convert: ryal ÷ 20 = dirham .

How do you understand? If the number looks 20 times too high, it's in ryal. The context helps: in traditional shops and among the elderly, ryal is very frequent; Dirham is used in supermarkets and documents. In some regions you can also feel Frank or Frank for the cent. In case of doubt, ask: b-d-drahəm? "In dirham"?

The petit taxi (ṭaksi ṣġir) travel around the city with a taximeter; the grand taxi (ṭaksi kbir) connects cities and is shared with other passengers.

Why so many foreign words? Morocco has been in contact for centuries with the Iberian peninsula and, in the twentieth century, under French and (northern) Spanish protectorate; amazigh, official language next to Arabic from 2011, is spoken by an important part of the population. Many Moroccans also pass to French in the same sentence (B2-17): ça va? · normal · d'accord are very frequent. Recognize a loan. If a word does not have a recognizable Arabic root, try to read it aloud "French" or "Spanish": l-biru → bureau; kuzina → cocina.
